description: Independent case corpus for the S10 cross-model comparison engine. Each case fixes its expected verdict, reason, preference and exclusions BEFORE the engine runs; the runner checks the engine against these expectations. The ten case classes ordered-1..ordered-10 are the owner-ordered classes of the S10 run instruction; the supplementary cases cover the remaining rule branches (full and pure-quality dominance, unqualified-only fields, adapter-boundary refusal, missing S9 evidence).
limits: Labels and expectations are constructed, not owner-reviewed; they fix what the engine must do, not what any real executor did.
All measurements are synthetic offline replay/fixture evidence; no provider was called, no credentials exist in this corpus, and the live_provider class is never exercised.
The corpus uses synthetic executor, provider and model identities; no statement about any real model or provider is derivable from it.
Instruction overhead numbers are constructed to exercise the derived-ratio invariant, not measured tokenizations.
A CANDIDATE_PREFERRED verdict in this corpus adopts nothing: it is a measured statement over synthetic material.

expectation.construction: Both candidates pass every gate with identical quality (0.90); cand_b is strictly cheaper on cost units, total tokens and tail latency, so it dominates on the cost dimensions alone — a cost preference between sufficiently qualified, regression-free candidates.
cand_b is cheaper and faster but measures a lower task success rate (0.85 vs 0.92); neither candidate dominates and the record invents no weighting — quality/cost trade-offs stay INCOMPARABLE.

cand_b dominates cand_a on every measured dimension (quality 0.95, half the cost, faster tail latency) AND carries a security regression count of 2. Security is absolute: b is excluded, its gains compensate nothing, and a alone is not a comparison result.
cand_b lacks the structured-output capability the task set requires; a different capability class is a different task class, so the field is incomparable rather than one candidate worse.

Neither candidate carries a qualification state beyond UNKNOWN or any qualification evidence; there is nothing qualified to optimize between, and missing evidence fails closed instead of comparing the unproven.
cand_b was measured against a different corpus revision (digest differs); candidates measured against different material are never silently normalized into one comparison.
cand_b was measured against a different success contract; identical-looking numbers over different success definitions are not comparable.
cand_b was measured under the fixture_replay class while the declared basis is offline_replay; measurements of different evidence classes do not mix into one record.

Both candidates report repeated runs that disagreed (quality spread across runs); the evidence exists but cannot support a preference, which is INCOMPARABLE, not missing. The stability gate excludes both candidates before the field-level INCOMPARABLE is declared; the exclusions are part of the record.
cand_b's measured runs failed with a provider outage; a failed execution is missing evidence for the whole comparison, so the record blocks instead of preferring the survivor on incomplete material.
cand_b carries no token totals and no cost units; the comparison metrics it would be preferred on are exactly the ones missing, and missing evidence fails closed.

cand_b's S9 comparison detected a regression (rgr_s10_cand_b=REGRESSION_DETECTED) even though its metrics dominate; it is excluded at the regression gate. cand_c, regression-free and cheaper than cand_a at equal quality, is preferred — optimization happens only among regression-free candidates.
cand_a is strictly better in quality AND strictly cheaper and faster; the preference reason is full dominance.

Both candidates carry qualification evidence but sit in DISQUALIFIED / QUALIFICATION_PENDING states; an unqualified executor never receives winner status, and with no winner-capable candidate there is no comparison result.

The declared optimization targets model-specific prompt shaping without binding it to an adapter boundary; model-specific optimization must stay at adapter boundaries, so the whole comparison refuses.

optimization_boundaries.detail: model-specific prompt tuning applied inside the shared core instead of at the executor adapter

expectation.construction: cand_a measures a strictly higher success rate at byte-identical cost and latency; the preference reason is quality dominance alone.
Neither candidate carries an S9 regression verdict at all; absence of a regression record is not cleanliness, and optimization without regression evidence is out of scope.
